This ended up being a lot harder than I first thought and resulted in me reinstalling 4! times due to my inability to chroot into an encrypted data pool. Anyway my system consists of a 2tb hd that is detected at /dev/sda and a 128gb ssd that detects at dev/sdb. I did a vanilla debian 9 stretch install and selected the guided partition with the encrypted volumes option. This created an encrypted volume on sda5 with two logical volumes, 1 for root and 1 for swap. The name of the volume group was $host-vg. Here is what I did to get everything working and booting:

First we create an encrypted volume on the ssd. Mine was detected at /dev/sdb

$ sudo cryptsetup luksFormat /dev/sdb

I called it "sdb_crypt"

$ sudo cryptsetup luksOpen /dev/sdb sdb_crypt

$ sudo pvcreate /dev/mapper/sdb_crypt

Find the volume group name of your main hard drive

$ sudo vgscan

Extend that volume group to include the ssd (replace "$host-vg" with your volume group name)

$ sudo vgextend $host-vg /dev/mapper/sdb_crypt

Create a cache-pool on the ssd using all space

$ sudo lvcreate --type cache-pool -l 100%pvs -n cache $host-vg /dev/mapper/sdb_crypt

$ sudo lvconvert --type cache --cachepool $host-vg/cache $host-vg/root

You now have your root data cached. Yeah. Getting your machine to boot again is a little more involved.

find the uuid of the ssd (mine was at /dev/sdb so "sdb" is in this statement):

$ ls -al /dev/disk/by-uuid/ | grep sdb | awk '{ print $9 }'

use the UUID of the ssd to make an additional entry in /etc/crypttab:

================================================

sdb_crypt UUID=${DISK_UUID} none luks,discard

================================================

Now the most difficult, you need to make sure there is support in the initramfs to support booting from a cache-pool encrypted drive. Basically you need a few modules and access to a script 'cache-check' in the initramfs in order to be able to boot.

Install a package to provide the cache-check script:

$ sudo apt install thin-provisioning-tools

Edit /etc/initramfs-tools/modules to add the following modules:

================================================

dm_cache

dm_cache_mq

dm_cache_smq

dm_persistent_data

dm_bufio

================================================

edit /etc/cryptsetup-initramfs/conf_hook and make sure the following parameter uncommented:

================================================

CRYPTSETUP=y

================================================

create /etc/initramfs-tools/hooks/cache_hook and past the following:

================================================

#!/bin/sh

PREREQ="lvm2"

prereqs() { echo "$PREREQ" }

case $1 in prereqs) prereqs exit 0 ;; esac

if [ ! -x /usr/sbin/cache_check ]; then exit 0 fi

. /usr/share/initramfs-tools/hook-functions

copy_exec /usr/sbin/cache_check

manual_add_modules dm_cache dm_cache_mq dm_cache_smq dm_persistent_data dm_bufio

================================================

make this script executable:

$ sudo chmod +x /etc/initramfs-tools/hooks/cache_hook

rebuild the initramfs

$ sudo update-initramfs -u

you should now be able to reboot. You will have to enter the passphrase for both sda5_crypt and sdb_crypt. I used the same pass phrase but it still requires me to enter twice. I am researching how to eliminate the double entry.
